en: Space launch vehicle technology shares its basic principles with missile technology, so it is a typical strategic technology whose transfer between countries is strictly controlled. Even if a country wants to buy it, no one will sell it, so the only option is to develop it independently. Korea gained experience through the launch of Naro in 2013, but because its first-stage rocket depended on Russian technology, it was hard to call that complete independence. The Nuri program, led by the Korea Aerospace Research Institute, is distinguished from earlier programs in that it aimed to secure the entire process—design, production, testing, and launch operation—with domestic technology.

The greatest obstacle in development was the 75-ton-class liquid engine. Liquid engines are counted as a technology that only a small number of countries possess, because their combustion process easily becomes unstable. The researchers completed the engine after hundreds of combustion tests, and they also secured clustering technology, which bundles four engines in the first stage to produce 300-ton-class thrust, as well as the technology to separate the stages during flight. Many Korean companies took part in the development, sharing the work of making and assembling parts, and this became an opportunity to lay the foundations of the space industry.

In the first launch in October 2021, Nuri reached its target altitude, but the third-stage engine shut down earlier than planned, and it failed to put the satellite model into orbit. The researchers identified the cause and improved the design, and in the second launch in June 2022, Nuri safely placed a performance verification satellite into orbit. In the third launch in May 2023, it delivered several working satellites into their planned orbits, proving its ability to provide launch services. With this, Korea became the seventh country in the world capable of launching satellites of more than one ton on its own.

The institutional foundation has also been put in place. In May 2024, the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) opened in Sacheon, South Gyeongsang Province, bringing together the space and aviation policies that had been divided among several ministries into one dedicated agency. As the center of gravity in space development shifts worldwide from governments to private companies, efforts are also under way to transfer Nuri's technology to the private sector and grow an industrial ecosystem.

Independence in launch vehicle technology is less a final goal in itself than a foundation that leads to satellite use, space exploration, and the growth of related industries. The ability to put a satellite into a desired orbit at a desired time supports fields closely tied to daily life, such as communications, weather observation, and land management. How to make use of the foundation created by Nuri's successful launches and the opening of KASA remains the next task for Korea's space development.

en: A genome refers to all of the genetic information that an organism carries. Genome editing is a technology that precisely cuts out or changes a specific position in the DNA sequence to control how genes function. Genetic scissors existed before CRISPR, but every time the target changed, a new protein had to be designed, which cost a great deal of time and money. In contrast, CRISPR-Cas9 is simple to design, low in cost, and highly accurate, so within about a decade of its appearance it established itself as the standard tool in laboratories worldwide. The fact that the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Charpentier and Doudna, who developed this technology, shows the scale of its impact.

CRISPR is originally an adaptive immune system that bacteria use against viruses. A bacterium stores pieces of an invading virus's DNA in its own genome, and when the same virus invades again, it identifies and cuts the intruder using RNA made from the stored information. In 2012, researchers simplified this system and published a method for cutting DNA at a desired position using only a guide RNA that binds to the target sequence and the Cas9 protein, a cutting enzyme. By making use of the process in which the cell repairs the cut DNA on its own, scientists can remove or fix a specific gene.

Applications are expanding rapidly. In medicine, research on treatments for diseases caused by genetic abnormalities is very active, and in 2023 a CRISPR-based treatment was approved for the first time in the world and began to be used to treat inherited blood diseases. In agriculture, the technology is used to develop crops that withstand drought and pests, and in basic research it has become a key tool for revealing what genes do. In Korea as well, basic science research institutes are carrying on genome editing research.

However, the technical limits and ethical issues are also clear. Errors can occur in which a location other than the target is cut, and the results of editing are hard to reverse. Above all, editing cells that are inherited by the next generation—such as sperm, eggs, and embryos—could leave effects on future generations that are hard to predict, so the international community strictly regulates it. This is because what technology can do and what it may be allowed to do are separate questions.

In the end, the future of genome editing technology will not be decided by scientific progress alone. Only when systems that verify safety and a social consensus that weighs risks against benefits are in place together can this technology become real hope for people suffering from disease. Scientific literacy—citizens' understanding of how the technology works and what is at stake—also forms the basis of that consensus.

challenge.q: 한 연구팀이 유전성 심장 질환을 일으키는 유전자를 배아 단계에서 교정하는 기술을 완성하고, 안전성도 입증되었으니 곧바로 병원에서 쓰자고 주장한다. 이에 대해 글쓴이가 보일 반응으로 가장 적절한 것은?

"이 기술의 목적은 질병으로 고통받는 사람들에게 실질적인 희망을 주는 것이므로, 치료 효과가 분명하다면 규제 논의보다 도입을 서둘러야 한다."
"배아 교정에서는 표적을 벗어나는 오류가 반드시 일어나므로, 어떤 경우에도 이 분야의 연구 자체를 중단해야 한다."

challenge.q: 이 글로부터 추론할 때, 크리스퍼-카스9이 이전 세대 유전자 가위보다 설계가 간단하고 비용이 낮은 근본적인 이유로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 카스9 단백질이 이전 기술의 단백질보다 크기가 작아 세포 안에 넣기 쉽기 때문이다.
세균의 적응 면역 체계를 그대로 옮겨 왔기 때문에 별도의 설계 과정 자체가 필요 없기 때문이다.
잘린 DNA를 세포가 스스로 복구하므로 과학자가 복구 장치를 따로 만들 필요가 없기 때문이다.
표적을 찾는 일을 단백질이 아닌 가이드 RNA가 맡으므로, 목표가 바뀌어도 절단 효소는 그대로 두고 RNA만 바꾸면 되기 때문이다.
challenge.explain: 첫 문단은 이전 기술이 목표가 바뀔 때마다 단백질을 새로 설계해야 해서 시간과 비용이 많이 들었다고 했고, 둘째 문단은 크리스퍼가 표적 염기서열에 결합하는 가이드 RNA와 절단 효소인 카스9의 조합임을 설명했다. 두 문단을 종합하면 표적 인식을 RNA가 담당하므로 목표가 바뀌어도 단백질을 다시 설계할 필요가 없다는 점이 설계 용이성과 저비용의 이유임을 추론할 수 있다. 세포의 자체 복구는 절단 이후 유전자를 없애거나 고치는 단계에 관한 설명이어서, 설계가 간단한 이유와는 무관하다.

en: Generative AI refers to artificial intelligence that creates new text, images, and sounds based on the data it has learned from. Most of the conversational AI services widely used today run on this technology. At the core of the technology for handling text is the large language model. A language model is a mathematical model that calculates the probability of which word will come after a given context, and its performance improved dramatically after a neural network architecture called the Transformer was proposed in 2017.

A language model breaks sentences into small units called tokens in order to process them. Training is carried out by repeating, countless times, the task of predicting the next token in vast amounts of text, and in this process parameters numbering from billions to hundreds of billions are adjusted. After pre-training, the model goes through additional training that refines it to follow human instructions. A typical method is to adjust the model by giving higher scores to the answers that people prefer. Through these two stages, the model comes to possess both knowledge and usefulness.

From this principle come both the abilities and the limits of language models. Because a model learns by compressing the knowledge and expressions contained in vast amounts of text, it shows outstanding performance in translation, summarizing, writing, and programming. However, this performance does not mean human-like understanding. The standard for its output is, after all, probabilistic plausibility, not whether something is true. Its representative limits include hallucination, in which it describes unfounded content convincingly; the reproduction of biases contained in its training data; and the absence of information from after its training period.

Social issues follow as well. Debates over the copyright of the texts used for training are under way around the world, and the risk that plausible false information created by AI may spread has also been raised. The enormous electricity and computing resources required to train large models are counted as a challenge too. In response, countries are putting in place systems for the safe use of AI. Research institutes in Korea and many other countries are also continuing research on the use and safety of artificial intelligence.

Language models operate in their own distinctive way—probability calculation—which is different from how humans understand language. If we know the principle, mature use becomes possible: instead of blindly trusting the results or rejecting them outright, we can make use of their strengths and make up for their limits through verification. The literacy to read technology is becoming a basic competence of our time.

en: Population structure is a framework that shows how a society's population is composed by age, gender, and other factors. Three factors—births, deaths, and international migration—determine population structure, and a key characteristic is that its changes are hard to reverse in a short period. Korea is a leading example of a society where low birth rates, with the number of newborns continuously falling, and population aging, with the share of people aged 65 and older growing, are progressing at the same time. A clear illustration is the population pyramid shifting from a bell shape to a shape that is wide at the top, and the future population projections of the Ministry of Data and Statistics also forecast that this trend will continue for a considerable time.

The primary background of population aging is the extension of life expectancy and the decline in the number of births. With advances in medical technology and living standards, people have come to live longer, while the number of newborns has fallen due to a combination of factors, including changing values about marriage and childbirth and the burdens of housing and child-rearing. As a result, a structure takes shape in which the share of the working-age population—people aged 15 to 64 who can work—shrinks, while the social cost of supporting the elderly population becomes relatively larger.

These changes spread across the economy and institutions as a whole. A smaller labor supply can affect the economy's growth potential, and systems run on contributions from the currently working generation, such as pensions and health insurance, face the task of redesigning the balance between burdens and benefits. This is because the ratio between those who pay taxes and those who receive welfare benefits changes. In education, adjustments to school operations to match the shrinking school-age population are being discussed, and in local communities, measures to maintain the functions of regions with declining populations are on the agenda.

The change does not mean only burdens. As consumption and health care demand among the elderly grow, the so-called silver industry—medical devices, care services, leisure industries, and more—is drawing attention as a new growth area. Discussions are also active about expanding continued employment and retraining so that older workers with accumulated experience can work longer. Some also expect that advances in technology may help fill the gaps in care and labor.

The government is pursuing population policies that cover responses to low birth rates, improvements in the quality of life of the elderly, and support for regions with declining populations. What matters is not to read population change only in the language of crisis, but to gradually redesign social systems on the basis of accurate statistics. The change in population structure is a reality already under way, and understanding its direction is a basic premise for preparing for the society of the future.

en: In a market economy, prices act as signals that allocate resources. Prices are set where supply and demand meet, and changes in prices alter the choices of producers and consumers. The overall price level of the economy as a whole—rather than individual prices—is called the price level, and its movements are measured by indicators such as the Consumer Price Index. When inflation appears, with prices rising continuously, the purchasing power of money falls; conversely, deflation, in which prices fall continuously, can shrink consumption and investment.

The causes of inflation are explained in two broad ways. One is demand-pull inflation, which appears when the economy improves and buying power grows stronger; the other is cost-push inflation, which appears when production costs, such as raw material prices or wages, rise. In real price movements, the two factors often work together, and factors from outside the country, such as international oil prices and exchange rates, also have an influence.

When prices change sharply, it becomes difficult for economic actors to predict the future, so central banks in every country take price stability as a core duty. The Bank of Korea operates monetary policy, influencing the money supply and interest rates in general by adjusting the base rate. Raising the base rate tends to slow borrowing and consumption, easing upward pressure on prices, while lowering it is expected to have the opposite effect. However, because there is a time lag before the effects of policy appear, careful judgment is required.

Wages are the price of labor as a factor of production, but they are not left purely to the market; the law guarantees a minimum level. The minimum wage system aims to stabilize the lives of low-paid workers, and it is grounded in the Constitution and the Minimum Wage Act. Every year the Minimum Wage Commission deliberates on it, with equal numbers of worker members, employer members, and public-interest members taking part in the discussion. The law requires that workers' cost of living, the wages of similar workers, labor productivity, and the income distribution ratio be considered, and once the government officially announces the deliberated proposal, it takes effect from January of the following year.

Prices and the minimum wage influence each other. When prices rise, the real value of the same wage falls, so the inflation rate becomes important data in the deliberation process, and changes in wages can in turn affect prices through production costs. In this way, prices and wages are determined on two axes: market principles and social agreement. Understanding these procedures and principles is a basic competence for reading economic news.

en: Thanks to its advantages of being light, easy to shape, and cheap, plastic has become a material used throughout modern civilization. However, that very durability is the source of an environmental problem. Plastic is broken down by microorganisms extremely slowly, so once it leaks into nature, it remains there for a very long time. A considerable share of the plastic produced worldwide has become waste, and part of it has accumulated in the sea after passing through rivers and coastal waters.

Plastic that flows into the ocean undergoes physical and chemical weathering. Ultraviolet rays weaken the molecular structure of plastic, and waves and sand break it into small pieces. The fragments smaller than 5 millimeters across created this way are microplastics, and some—like the fine particles that come from facial cleansers or textiles—are made small from the beginning and released that way. Because microplastics are so small, recovering them is practically impossible, and they spread along ocean currents and have been detected even in the open ocean, the deep sea, and the polar regions.

The effects on the ecosystem are multi-layered. Large pieces of waste cause entanglement and swallowing accidents among marine animals, and so-called ghost fishing, in which abandoned fishing gear keeps catching fish, also causes losses to fishery resources. Microplastics are ingested even by small creatures such as plankton and move along the food chain, and they have been detected in the seafood and salt that people eat. However, how they affect the human body is still an area where research is in progress, and the scientific community is carefully building up evidence.

Responses can be organized into four layers: preventing release, collection, recycling, and international cooperation. The government and the Korea Marine Environment Management Corporation collect trash from coastal waters and the seabed and improve the systems for managing fishing gear. Policies that encourage the use of easily recyclable materials at the production stage and reduce the use of single-use plastics are also spreading. The international community is continuing negotiations to establish a binding agreement that covers the entire life cycle of plastic pollution.

The essence of the marine plastic problem is that the cost of convenience is transferred across time and space to the ecosystem as a whole. Since the sea has no borders, the efforts of one country alone have limits, and an approach that redesigns the loop running from production to disposal is required. Only when individual actions that reduce consumption and institutional change work together can the flow of plastic heading toward the sea be reduced.

en: The Earth's atmosphere lets energy from the Sun pass through, while absorbing part of the infrared radiation given off by the surface and releasing it again. This process is the greenhouse effect, and greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane play that role. The problem is that since industrialization, the burning of fossil fuels and the destruction of forests have rapidly raised the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, upsetting the Earth's energy balance and pushing up its average temperature. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has made it clear that human activity is the main cause of global warming.

In response, the international community agreed through the Paris Agreement to hold the rise in the global average temperature to well below 2 degrees above pre-industrial levels, and if possible within 1.5 degrees. Carbon neutrality, also called net zero, refers to a state in which the amount of greenhouse gases emitted by human activity equals the amount absorbed and removed, so that net emissions become zero. Many countries, including Korea, have declared the goal of carbon neutrality by 2050 and have put laws and plans in place.

At the center of this transition is the power sector. Solar power uses the photoelectric effect: when light strikes a solar cell, a semiconductor device, electrons move and an electric current is produced. Wind power obtains electricity by using the kinetic energy of the wind to turn a turbine. Neither method requires fuel costs, and both emit almost no greenhouse gases during power generation. As technological progress and mass production have steadily lowered the cost of generation, renewable energy facilities are expanding rapidly around the world.

However, a power system centered on renewable energy faces challenges that must be solved. Sunlight and wind cannot be controlled by humans, so power output is intermittent, varying with time and weather. Making up for this requires storage such as energy storage systems (ESS) and pumped-storage hydropower, systems for adjusting demand, and expanded transmission networks that move electricity between regions. Public acceptance of sites for power facilities, and the recycling of used panels and batteries, are also counted among the problems to solve.

Carbon neutrality is not a task for the power sector alone. It also requires switching fuels in industrial processes, improving insulation and efficiency in buildings, electrifying transportation, and preserving carbon sinks such as forests and tidal flats. Improving efficiency, which means getting the same benefit while using less energy, is regarded as the most reliable way to cut emissions. Carbon neutrality is not a goal achieved by any single technology; it is a long-term task in which technology, institutions, and ways of living must change together.

en: What does a record need in order to earn the trust of later generations? Depending only on the conscience of the record-keeper has its limits. Joseon tried to solve this problem not through personal virtue but through institutions. The result was the Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty, which contains about 470 years of history under 25 kings, from Taejo to Cheoljong. The Veritable Records were not personal biographies of kings but official state records covering politics, the economy, and culture as a whole.

The first device for trust was the court historian system. Historians sat in on the meetings where the king and his officials discussed state affairs and recorded their words and actions in drafts called sacho. The key lay in the principle that guaranteed the independence of the records. Even the king was not allowed to read the sacho, and as a rule, what a historian had written was not to be called into question. By making it impossible for those in power to control the records, Joseon was able to maintain the tradition of jikpil, writing the facts exactly as they were.

The second device was a strict compilation procedure. There was a principle that the Veritable Records were compiled only after the king in question had died. When a king passed away, a temporary office called the Sillokcheong was set up, and it gathered, compared, and verified records from many offices, including the sacho and the Diaries of the Royal Secretariat. By cross-checking multiple records instead of relying on a single source, the compilers raised the accuracy of the contents. After compilation, the sacho went through secho, being washed in water to erase them, a measure to prevent sensitive records from leaking out and leading to political revenge.

The third device was distributed storage. In the early Joseon period, the same records were divided among the Chunchugwan in Seoul and three archives in the provinces. When the Japanese invasions of the 1590s burned all the copies except the one in the Jeonju archive, Joseon printed several new sets based on the surviving records and moved the archives to hard-to-reach places such as Ganghwa Island and Mount Taebaek. The risk was spread out so that a disaster in any one place would not mean the loss of the entire record.

Thanks to these institutional devices, the Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty are regarded as a rare example of the systematic, long-term recording of a single dynasty's history. Because they contain information on all areas of society, including astronomy, weather, and disasters as well as politics and diplomacy, they serve as research material for many academic fields. In 1997, UNESCO officially recognized their value by inscribing them in the Memory of the World register. What the Veritable Records ultimately show is that the objectivity and reliability of a record come not from an individual's good will but from the institutions that support it.

en: Most of the world's writing systems took shape naturally, changing little by little over long stretches of time. As a result, scripts whose creator, date of creation, and design principles are all known are rare in the world. Hunminjeongeum, created by King Sejong in 1443 and proclaimed in 1446, is exceptional in this respect. Not only are its creator and time of creation clear, but the principles on which the script was designed are systematically recorded in its commentary, the Hunminjeongeum Haerye.

The consonant system of Hunminjeongeum is based on observation of how speech sounds are produced. The five basic consonants imitate the shapes of the speech organs at the places where the sounds are made: ㄱ, the root of the tongue blocking the throat; ㄴ, the tip of the tongue touching the upper gums; ㅁ, the mouth; ㅅ, a tooth; and ㅇ, the throat. Sounds made at the same place but pronounced more strongly were written by adding strokes to the basic letters. Because the form of each letter reflects where and how the sound is articulated, Hunminjeongeum is regarded as a script that carries phonetic information within its writing system.

The design of the vowels applied the principle of combining three basic letters representing heaven (ㆍ), earth (ㅡ), and human (ㅣ). When these basic letters are combined according to fixed rules, the remaining vowels are formed systematically. This method of writing a wide variety of sounds with a minimum of elements and clear rules of combination can be called an efficient design that creates many things from few parts. The way consonants and vowels are grouped and written in syllable blocks also makes the structure of the sounds visible.

For a long time, these principles of creation were a matter of guesswork. When the Hunminjeongeum Haerye, the book that explains the principles, was discovered in Andong, North Gyeongsang Province, in 1940, the principles behind the letters were finally confirmed. The Haerye describes the reason each of the twenty-eight letters was created and how they were to be used. Its discovery is considered an event that greatly changed the direction of Hangeul studies. The book has been designated a National Treasure of Korea, and in 1997 it was inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World register.

Today, linguists regard Hunminjeongeum as an original script designed on the basis of an analysis of the speech organs and the nature of sounds. A writing system made easy to learn lowered the barrier to written communication, and in the information age, its principle of combining consonant and vowel letters has also proved an advantage for entering text on mobile phones and computers. The case of Hunminjeongeum shows that a writing system need not be merely a product of custom; it can be the object of design based on principles.

en: The form of content changes according to the character of the medium that carries it. Korean webtoons are a clear example of this change. In the early 2000s, as the print comics market shrank, internet portals opened spaces where comics were serialized for free, and a new form called the webtoon emerged. Freed from the physical limits of paper, webtoons reorganized the grammar of comics to fit the media environment of the digital screen.

At the heart of this reorganization is the vertical-scroll format. Unlike print comics, which arrange scenes page by page, webtoons place their story on one long flow running from top to bottom. Since the speed at which readers scroll the screen becomes the speed at which they read the story, authors control the passage of time and the level of tension by adjusting the size of the panels and the length of the blank spaces. This format matched the narrow, tall screens of smartphones, and as mobile devices spread, webtoons became a part of everyday content.

On the industrial side, webtoons formed an ecosystem of their own. The partial-payment model, in which readers can wait and read for free but must pay to read ahead, drew readers who were used to free content into the paid market. The way works are created also changed: in addition to individual authors working alone, the division of labor expanded, with collaboration between story writers and artists and the participation of production studios and agencies. Platforms took charge of distributing works and sharing revenue, placing themselves at the center of the ecosystem. Meanwhile, as the industry has grown, discussions about authors' working conditions and fair contracts have been taking place as well.

Another pillar of the webtoon industry is the expansion of intellectual property, or IP. Webtoons with proven stories and established fan bases are used as source material for dramas, films, games, and other media. A reinforcing effect also appears: when a screen adaptation based on a webtoon succeeds, more readers go back to the original. This way of building value as one story moves across many media has made webtoons an important supplier of stories for the video industry.

Korean webtoon platforms have expanded their services into many language regions, spreading the vertical-scroll format throughout the world's digital comics market. Discovering local authors and offering works in local languages goes beyond simple export; it can be called the transplanting of the format itself. The case of webtoons shows that when changes in the media environment are treated as an opportunity rather than a constraint, innovation in the form of content can lead to the expansion of an industry.

en: Space is a radiation environment in which high-energy particles fly about without pause. Typical examples are particles released by solar activity and galactic cosmic rays arriving from outside the solar system. Life on the Earth's surface is largely protected from their effects by a double shield: the thick atmosphere and the Earth's magnetic field. The lunar surface, with almost no atmosphere and only a feeble magnetic field, is a different story. Not only does space radiation reach it directly, but secondary radiation, such as the neutrons produced when particles collide with the lunar soil, is added on top.

Exposure to radiation damages the body's cells and genetic material, threatening the health of astronauts who stay for long periods. For crewed exploration programs that aim to send people to stay on the Moon, therefore, precise measurements of the radiation environment on the lunar surface are essential. Only by knowing which particles arrive, with how much energy, and in what quantities can scientists decide on the shielding design of spacesuits and living facilities, or the limits on how long astronauts can stay, in a scientific way.

The lunar surface space radiation detector LVRAD, being developed under the leadership of the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute, is a science payload that answers this need. Made up of a device that measures radiation dose and energy distribution and a neutron spectrometer, it aims to assess the radiation environment on the surface of the Moon's south pole and its effects on the human body. Because the south pole may hold water ice, many countries are watching it as a candidate site for crewed exploration, which makes radiation data from this region especially valuable.

What deserves attention is how this instrument will travel to the Moon. In August 2026, the Korea AeroSpace Administration signed an implementing arrangement with the U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) to send LVRAD through NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program. Under CLPS, instead of building landers itself, NASA entrusts the transport of scientific instruments to landers developed by private companies. It is, in effect, a new division of labor in space development, in which government agencies focus on science missions while the private sector handles transportation.

If all goes as planned, LVRAD will complete its flight model by 2027 and be shipped to the United States, then arrive at the Moon's south pole aboard a lander launching in 2030. The launch date, however, may shift depending on NASA's schedule. A Korean observation instrument will produce basic data for lunar exploration within a framework of international cooperation, and this carries the meaning that Korean science and technology is taking part in preparing for the era of crewed lunar exploration.

en: The greenhouse gases that companies release while producing goods impose a cost on society as a whole in the form of climate change. Yet that cost is not reflected in market prices, so the emitters themselves pay nothing for it. In economics, this phenomenon, in which the costs or benefits of an activity are passed on to third parties, is called an "externality." The emissions trading scheme is a system that puts a price on pollution, bringing this hidden cost into companies' profit-and-loss calculations.

The backbone of the scheme is the "cap and trade" method. The government first sets a cap, the total amount of greenhouse gases that may be emitted during a given period. It then issues allowances up to that limit and allocates them to companies. One allowance is the right to emit greenhouse gases equivalent to one ton of carbon dioxide. Because the total is fixed by the system, the combined emissions of all participating companies cannot exceed the set limit.

The refinement of this scheme lies in letting the market decide where the reductions take place. Companies whose reduction costs are low cut their own emissions and earn money by selling their leftover allowances. Companies whose reduction costs are high choose to buy allowances instead of replacing their facilities at unreasonable expense. As a result, society as a whole achieves the targeted amount of reduction at the lowest cost. When allowance prices rise, the incentive to invest in low-carbon technology grows, and the value of companies that hold reduction technology rises along with it.

Korea introduced a nationwide emissions trading scheme in 2015. The scheme covers about 74% of the country's greenhouse gas emissions, and about 770 companies subject to allocation are taking part in the fourth planning period, which runs from 2026 to 2030. Industries with large emissions, such as power generation, steel, and petrochemicals, are the main participants. Allowances are traded on the Korea Exchange, and their prices move with allocation levels, the economy, and policy changes; recently they have also swung sharply.

Of course, there are challenges. If more allowances are allocated than needed, prices fall and the incentive to reduce emissions weakens; if prices soar, the burden on companies grows. Therefore, how strictly the cap is set and how the share of paid allocation, in which allowances are sold rather than given out for free, is adjusted will decide the success or failure of the scheme. Designing the market so that the price placed on pollution leads to real reductions is still a work in progress. This discussion is also the process by which our society decides who will bear how much of the cost of climate change.

en: It is not only the air that global warming has heated. Most of the extra heat trapped by greenhouse gases is stored in the ocean. As a result, extreme events corresponding to heatwaves on land also occur in the sea, and these are marine heatwaves. A marine heatwave is a phenomenon in which the water temperature in a particular sea area remains unusually high, compared with the normal values for that time of year, for five days or longer. Scientists generally identify a marine heatwave when the water temperature stays above the top 10% of the observation records of the past thirty years. Since the standard is relative to region and season, marine heatwaves can occur even in winter seas.

According to the analysis 'Climate Characteristics and Future Outlook of the Seas around Korea,' released by the Korea Meteorological Administration in August 2026, marine heatwaves in Korean waters occurred for an average of 83.3 days per year over the last decade (2016-2025), 3.7 times the normal level. Over the same period, the average sea surface temperature was 18.1 degrees, 0.7 degrees above normal. The outlook for the future is even clearer. Although it depends on greenhouse gas emission scenarios, marine heatwaves could increase to around 300 days a year by the end of the twenty-first century. Most of the year, in other words, would be in a state of 'ocean heatwave.'

A rise of a few degrees in water temperature may seem trivial, but for marine creatures, whose body temperature follows the water around them, it is a matter of survival. When a marine heatwave strikes, cold-water fish species shift their habitats northward, while seaweeds and shellfish that cannot move sometimes die off in masses. As the species that fishermen catch change, the landscape of the fishing industry changes as well. Fish on aquaculture farms, confined to one place, cannot escape the hot water, which often leads to large-scale die-offs in summer. A marine heatwave thus shakes marine ecosystems and the fisheries industry at the same time.

The effects do not end in the sea. A heated ocean supplies the atmosphere with vast amounts of heat and water vapor, fueling heatwaves and torrential rain on land and helping typhoons move north while keeping their strength. A feedback occurs in which changes in the ocean disturb the climate in turn. In response, countries monitor water temperatures in real time with satellites and observation buoys, and issue warnings when high water temperatures are expected so that fish farms can prepare in advance. Above all, reducing greenhouse gas emissions is considered the most fundamental response that can lower the frequency and intensity of future marine heatwaves.

Marine heatwaves are a subject that scientists have only recently begun to study in earnest, and for that very reason the field has much left to uncover. From marine scientists who diagnose the state of the ocean with satellite data, and climate researchers who calculate the future climate under different scenarios, to fisheries experts who develop species and farming technologies suited to a changed sea, the warming ocean is a place where many careers meet. The task of turning the crisis of the ocean into an opportunity remains in the hands of the generation reading this article.

en: Colorectal cancer is a disease whose treatment outcomes improve dramatically with early detection, yet the barriers to screening are not low. Colonoscopy is accurate, but the bowel preparation and its invasive nature make it burdensome, while the convenient fecal occult blood test has a sensitivity of only 70 to 80 percent. This gap between burden and accuracy is one reason why many people put off getting screened.

A promising candidate for narrowing this gap is the liquid biopsy. As cells in the body die, they release DNA fragments into the bloodstream; these are known as cell-free DNA. Fragments derived from cancer cells differ subtly from those of normal cells in characteristics such as fragment length, end structures, and their distribution across the genome. They are, in effect, traces that cancer cells leave in the blood. The problem is that these differences are scattered through vast amounts of data, making them difficult for humans to read directly.

This is where artificial intelligence comes in. On August 27, 2026, a research team at Asan Medical Center announced a study that analyzed blood samples from 1,677 people, including 302 colorectal cancer patients, 108 patients with advanced polyps, and 1,267 normal controls. Next-generation sequencing read the genetic information of the cell-free DNA, and an AI model was trained to learn the patterns unique to cancer patients from the fragments' characteristics. As a result, the sensitivity for diagnosing colorectal cancer was 90.4 percent and the specificity 94.7 percent, with strong performance across stages, including 84.2 percent for stage 1 and 100 percent for stage 4. The findings were published in the American Journal of Gastroenterology.

Making a test easier is not merely a matter of convenience. If a simple blood draw could screen for high-risk individuals, the barrier to screening would fall, and the probability of detecting cancer at an easily treatable stage would rise accordingly. Still, these results remain at the stage of suggested possibility. A liquid biopsy is a screening test that filters for the likelihood of cancer, not a confirmatory test, so even a positive result must be verified through colonoscopy and biopsy. The sensitivity for detecting advanced polyps, a precancerous stage, remained at 58.3 percent, and larger-scale validation is still needed before the test can enter actual screening programs.

A diagnostic technology like this cannot be completed by any single profession. Doctors who see patients and generate clinical data, life scientists who uncover the biological characteristics of cell-free DNA, and medical AI developers who design models and verify their performance each contributed their expertise. At this moment, when new technologies are being born at the boundary where medicine, life science, and computer science meet, that boundary zone is also where the jobs of the future are being created.

en: One of the most important principles in heritage conservation is 'authenticity' — the idea that a site should keep, as far as possible, the original materials, techniques, and forms it was built with. This applies equally to Jongmyo, inscribed as a World Heritage site in 1995, and Changdeokgung, inscribed in 1997. Beneath their splendid wooden architecture, it is stone that has supported the buildings, forming their platforms, terraces, and retaining walls. Yet exactly what kind of rock these stones are, and where they came from, had long remained without systematic documentation.

Since 2023, the National Research Institute of Cultural Heritage of the Korea Heritage Service has been answering this question through its scientific survey project on the stone heritage of Seoul's palaces and Jongmyo. Researchers surveyed all 4,421 stones — 2,922 at Changdeokgung and 1,499 at Jongmyo — and released a report on the findings in 2026. They also produced 'rock maps' that visually mark the rock types on measured drawings of the stone structures, so that anyone can see at a glance which stone was used in which position.

The analysis showed that the stones of both sites are overwhelmingly pale pink granite: more than 90% at Changdeokgung and over 99% at Jongmyo. Granite is a rock formed when magma cools slowly deep underground; because it is hard and can be quarried in large blocks, it has long been widely used in construction. The researchers also confirmed that the same type of pale pink granite is distributed across the mountains around Seoul, including Inwangsan, Ansan, Bukaksan, Bukhansan, and Buramsan.

The reason quarry information matters lies in repair and restoration. Depending on where it was formed, stone differs in mineral composition and texture, and therefore in color, strength, and even the speed at which it weathers. If a damaged block is replaced with stone of different properties, the appearance will not match, and over time it will change differently from the stones around it, undermining the authenticity of the site. This is why the report includes mineralogical and geochemical analyses of granite from the Seoul and Pocheon areas — baseline data for selecting substitute stones that best match the originals in future repairs.

This survey is a case of natural science reaching deep into heritage studies, a field once seen as belonging to the humanities. Petrology reveals what the stones are, and conservation science turns that knowledge into techniques for protecting heritage. A conservation scientist analyzes the materials of cultural heritage, diagnoses the causes of damage, and decides how to treat it — work that requires an interdisciplinary grounding spanning history and art history as well as chemistry and geology. Tracing a centuries-old stone back to its home turns out to be a way of protecting the future of a World Heritage site.

en: Even for the same electricity, the cost of supplying it differs depending on where it is used. Some electricity is inevitably lost as heat while flowing through power lines, and sending it far away requires building and maintaining a transmission network of towers and substations. In Korea, nuclear plants and renewable energy facilities are concentrated in the southern regions while consumption is concentrated in the capital area, so these costs are especially large. Until now, however, industrial electricity rates have been the same everywhere in the country, and regional differences in supply costs have not been reflected in the price.

On August 26, 2026, the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Korea Electric Power Corporation held a public hearing and unveiled a draft design for a regional industrial electricity pricing system. The plan adds a new 'regional adjustment rate' to the current structure of basic and usage charges, divides the country into four zones based on the structure of the power grid, and then subdivides it into eleven regions in consideration of balanced growth. In the southern region, where generation facilities are concentrated, rates would fall by up to 18 won per kilowatt-hour, about 10% of the 2025 average industrial price of 181.9 won; the northern capital area would see cuts of up to 10 won and the central region up to 15 won. The southern capital area, where consumption is concentrated, would stay around its current level, and Jeju was excluded from the plan.

Behind this design lies the economic principle that a price is a signal. If rates vary by region, semiconductor plants and data centers that consume large amounts of power will treat electricity rates as one variable when choosing a location. The government expects this signal to draw industrial facilities toward regions near power plants, reducing the burden of transmission investment and transmission losses while contributing to balanced regional development.

Yet open questions remain. Because a company's location depends on many factors besides electricity rates, such as securing workers, transportation and logistics, and distance to markets, it is uncertain whether the rate gap will lead to actual relocation. Some worry that regions may clash over who gains and who loses, while industry groups call for swift implementation and additional support. Above all, the plan is not yet a confirmed system. Only after the draft is refined with opinions from the hearing and procedures such as official notices and revisions to the rate terms are completed will it become a real system.

A single electricity bill contains engineering, economics, and law at once. Engineers who design power grids that reduce transmission losses, business strategists who analyze rates and site conditions to decide where factories and data centers belong, and policy and legal experts who translate the pricing system into the language of notices and terms are all connected to this draft. Reading the principles that move behind the signal called price: that is the shared starting point of these careers.

en: On August 27, 2026, the Ministry of Education announced that classroom teachers would take the lead in developing both the learning materials and the textbooks for the artificial intelligence (AI) subjects being introduced in schools. Sixteen subjects were selected through an open call—six in elementary school, two in middle school, and eight in high school—and this is the first time the state has supported textbook development for AI subjects at the national level. It offers a new answer to an old question: who should make our textbooks?

Korean school textbooks are classified as government-designated, government-authorized, or locally approved, according to how they are developed and screened. Government-designated textbooks are developed directly by the state, which holds the copyright. Authorized textbooks are produced by publishers and must pass a screening by a state-appointed institution. Approved textbooks are endorsed by provincial offices of education for use in schools; they are used when no designated or authorized textbook exists or when supplements are needed. Because their procedures are relatively flexible, they are well suited to reflecting the characteristics of newly created subjects. This is precisely why the new AI textbooks take the approved-textbook route.

Behind teacher-led development lies a long-standing difficulty in the field. Schools offered AI-related courses, but with no official textbooks, teachers bore the burden of producing their own materials every semester. In this project, classroom teachers participate as authors and lead the entire process, from curriculum analysis and unit design to writing the manuscript. When the book is written by people who know where students stumble and which classroom activities actually work, its suitability for real classrooms rises.

Another challenge for AI subjects is speed. Developing and reviewing a textbook takes time, yet AI technology keeps changing in the meantime. The chosen structure therefore has two parts: the main volume carries core concepts and principles that endure, while the latest technology trends and hands-on cases are separated into booklets or web-based materials that are updated continuously. The ministry also stressed that in such a fast-moving field, textbooks must be developed in a form flexible enough to hold the newest content in a timely manner.

The textbooks will be piloted in schools in the first semester of 2027, refined, and reviewed for approval by provincial offices of education in the second half of the year, before entering classrooms in March 2028. The people who will open these new textbooks are today's elementary, middle, and high school students. Teachers who design learning, edtech developers who build learning technology, and content creators who shape knowledge into engaging materials—education in the age of AI is opening a new stage for many professions, and you are its first main actor.

en: A work of art starts moving toward its own disappearance the moment it is finished. Pigments fade under light, paper oxidizes and yellows, metal corrodes, and cracks spread across the surface of an oil painting. The activity that slows this process and extends the life of a work is conservation science. It demands the eye of an art historian, who asks when and with what intention a work was made, and the hand of a chemist, who analyzes materials and selects treatments. It is a rare field that cannot be reduced to either art or science alone.

Conservation treatment rests on one long-standing principle: reversibility. Whatever is done today must be undoable when a better method appears. Because of this principle, a conservator does not begin by touching the work. A condition survey records where and how badly the piece is damaged, and that record becomes the ground for deciding how to treat it. Leaving a documented reason matters more than the result of the treatment, because the next custodian of the work must be able to review today's choice and reverse it.

In practice, prevention occupies a larger share of the work than repair. Korea's National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, the only national institution of its kind in the country, cares for some 8,000 works across four fields: paper, oil painting, sculpture and craft, and material analysis. Galleries and storage rooms are held at 18 to 22 degrees, with relative humidity between 50 and 70 percent. Too much moisture brings mold and buckling; too little causes surfaces to flake. Lighting limits follow the material. Oil paintings are kept at 150 lux or less, ink and watercolor paintings at 100 lux, dyed works and prints at 80 lux, while metal and stone, which tolerate light well, may be shown at up to 1,500 lux. Physical properties, not price or fame, draw the line.

Contemporary art unsettles this system. Nam June Paik's The More, the Better is a five-tier tower of 1,003 cathode ray tube monitors standing 18.5 meters high, installed at the museum's Gwacheon building in 1988. It was shut down in 2018 over fire risk from aging parts, and in 2019 the museum began a three-year restoration under the rule that the original form would be kept as far as possible, with replacement technology introduced only where unavoidable. A detailed survey found that only 26 percent of the monitors still worked. Seven hundred and thirty-seven damaged units were repaired with secondhand parts, while 266 at the top, beyond saving, kept their outer shells and received flat panels inside. The project cost 3.7 billion won, and the tower was switched back on in September 2022.

The problem does not end with the restoration. To protect the work, the museum limits operation to two hours a day, four days a week. Is The More, the Better still that work when the power is off? Are the 266 monitors, shells preserved and interiors replaced, still Paik's? Whether the authenticity of a work lies in its original form or in its capacity to run is a question technology cannot answer. That is why the museum opened its first training program for young conservators in 2026. Conserving contemporary art can no longer be handled by craft skill alone.

부채를 들고 몸짓으로 장면을 그려 보이는 발림이다.
무대 장치는 없고 연기자도 한 명뿐이지만,
이 세 가지를 오가며 수십 명이 등장하는 이야기를 몇 시간 동안 이어 간다.
부채 하나가 펼쳐지면 문이 되고 접히면 붓이나 지팡이가 된다.
적은 도구로 많은 장면을 만들어 내는 방식이다.
가장 느린 진양조에서 중모리, 중중모리, 자진모리를 지나
슬픔을 길게 늘여야 할 대목에서는 느린 장단이,
쫓고 쫓기는 대목에서는 빠른 장단이 쓰인다.
고수는 이 장단을 짚어 주는 동시에
소리의 완급을 조절하고 추임새로 기운을 끌어올린다.
「일고수 이명창」, 곧 첫째가 고수이고 둘째가 명창이라는 옛말은
반주자로 보이는 자리가 실은 공연의 축이라는 사실을 말해 준다.
이는 감상의 표현을 넘어 판을 함께 만드는 행위로 여겨진다.
무대와 객석이 분명히 나뉘고 침묵이 예의가 되는 공연과 견주면 차이가 뚜렷하다.
판소리에서 듣는 사람은 구경꾼이 아니라 판의 한 축이다.
판마다 다른 공연이 되는 까닭이 여기에 있다.
판소리는 원래 열두 마당이었으나 소리가 길어지면서
춘향가, 심청가, 흥보가, 수궁가, 적벽가 다섯 마당으로 정착했다.
2003년 유네스코 「인류 구전 및 무형유산 걸작」으로 선정된 뒤
무형유산은 건물이나 그림과 달리 사람의 몸에 담겨 전해진다.
가르치고 배우는 사람이 끊기면 유산도 함께 사라진다.
판소리를 지킨다는 말이 결국 사람을 잇는 일인 이유다.

국가무형문화재 지정 제도의 변천
부채를 활용한 연기 기술의 발달사
questions.explain: 글은 「판」이 세 쪽으로 성립한다는 점에서 출발해 청중의 위치를 특징으로 짚고, 무형유산이 사람을 통해 전해진다는 결론으로 닫는다.

questions.q: 문맥에 비추어 「조율」의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?

questions.q: 「판소리를 보존하려면 음원과 영상으로 완벽히 기록해 두면 충분하다」는 주장에 대한 이 글의 관점으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 기록이 남으면 전승이 끊겨도 무형유산은 유지된다
기록은 유용하지만 무형유산은 사람을 통해 전해지므로 가르치고 배우는 관계가 끊기면 사라진다

questions.explain: 글은 무형유산이 사람의 몸에 담겨 전해지며 가르치고 배우는 사람이 끊기면 유산도 사라진다고 했다. 또 판마다 공연이 달라진다고도 했으므로, 고정된 기록만으로는 대체되지 않는다.

challenge.q: 글쓴이가 「판은 물리적인 공간이 아니다」라고 한 진술의 전제를 가장 잘 짚은 것은?
choices: 공연장이 좁아도 상관없다는 전제
예술의 완성 여부를 참여자의 관계로 판단한다는 전제
야외 공연이 실내 공연보다 낫다는 전제
무대 장치가 예술의 수준을 결정한다는 전제
challenge.explain: 글은 세 쪽이 함께 있어야 판이 성립한다고 본다. 곧 공연의 완성을 장소나 장치가 아니라 참여자들 사이의 관계로 판단하는 관점이 깔려 있다.

challenge.q: 이 글의 관점을 학교 공연에 적용할 때 가장 알맞은 제안은?
choices: 관객은 끝까지 조용히 듣도록 안내한다
무대 장치 예산을 늘려 사실적으로 꾸민다
관객이 호응을 보낼 수 있는 대목을 미리 알려 함께 만들게 한다
공연을 녹화해 두고 실황은 생략한다
challenge.explain: 판소리는 청중의 응답을 공연의 일부로 본다. 관객이 함께 만들 여지를 두는 것이 이 관점의 적용이다. 침묵을 요구하거나 실황을 없애는 것은 반대 방향이다.

en: Pansori is a traditional Korean performing art in which one singer unfolds a long narrative to a drummer's beat. It took its present shape in the late Joseon period and has continued to this day. The name joins pan, a gathering, and sori, sound. Yet the pan is not a physical space. A singer, a drummer, and an audience must be present together for a pan to exist. This is where any understanding of pansori begins.

The singer works with three means. Chang is sung melody. Aniri is speech that sets the scene and carries the dialogue. Ballim is gesture, drawn in the air with a fan. There is no scenery and only one performer, yet the three together can sustain a story of dozens of characters for hours. Opened, the fan is a door. Closed, it is a brush or a walking stick. Few objects are made to serve many scenes.

Rhythm regulates the pace of the narrative. Jinyangjo is the slowest, followed by jungmori, jungjungmori, and jajinmori, and hwimori is the fastest. Slow patterns stretch a passage of grief, while quick ones drive a chase. The drummer marks these patterns, controls how the sound quickens or eases, and lifts the singer with short cries. An old saying places the drummer first and the singer second, which tells us that the seat that looks like accompaniment is in fact the axis of the performance.

The most striking feature is where the audience stands. Listeners answer the sound with short cries of praise. The word for them means a sound that lifts a person up. This is treated not merely as appreciation but as an act of building the pan. The contrast is clear with performances in which stage and seats are firmly divided and silence is good manners. Here the listener is not a spectator but one axis of the pan. That is why the same singer performing the same passage produces a different show at every pan.

Pansori once had twelve stories, but as each grew longer five remained: Chunhyangga, Simcheongga, Heungboga, Sugungga, and Jeokbyeokga. Korea designated it a national intangible heritage in 1964. UNESCO selected it as a masterpiece of oral and intangible heritage in 2003, and it was merged into the representative list in 2008. Unlike a building or a painting, intangible heritage is carried in human bodies. If those who teach and those who learn are cut off, the heritage disappears with them. That is why protecting pansori is finally a matter of keeping people connected.

L4.title: 옮길 수 없는 말 앞에서 — 번역가의 판단
paragraphs: 그런데 이 상의 심사위원들은 한국어를 읽지 못한다.
그들이 읽은 것은 영어와 스웨덴어로 옮겨진 판본이었다.
작품이 국경을 넘으려면 누군가 그것을 다른 언어로 다시 써야 한다.
번역은 원작에 딸린 부수적인 절차가 아니라
작품이 세계 독자와 만나는 유일한 경로다.
한강의 「채식주의자」를 영어로 옮긴 이는 영국 번역가 데버라 스미스다.
영어권 출판 시장에서 한국 문학이 거의 다루어지지 않는다는 판단에서 나온 선택이었다.
한국어를 배운 지 삼 년째인 2012년, 그는 이 소설의 번역에 착수했다.
그는 앞부분 스무 쪽가량을 옮겨 영국의 한 독립 출판사에 보내며 출간을 제안했고,
책이 나온 뒤에는 평론가와 독자에게 직접 알리는 일까지 맡았다.
2016년 이 책은 부커상 인터내셔널 부문을 수상했다.
이 부문은 그해부터 작가와 번역가에게 상을 함께 주기 시작했다.
그 사회의 위계와 관계, 생활 습관이 함께 붙어 있다.
비슷해 보이는 영어 낱말로 대치하는 순간
스미스는 이런 어휘를 번역하지 않고 한국어 발음 그대로 두는 쪽을 택했다.
그 낯섦 자체가 다른 사회를 알리는 표지가 된다.
이 번역은 뒤에 국내 학계에서 논쟁의 대상이 되었다.
주어가 생략된 한국어 문장을 잘못 옮겼고,
원문에 없는 문장을 넣어 인물의 인상이 달라졌다는 지적이 이어졌다.
번역이 아니라 「다시 쓰기」에 가깝다는 비판도 나왔다.
두 언어는 문법과 낱말, 구두점의 무게까지 다르므로
글자 그대로의 번역은 애초에 존재할 수 없다고 반박했다.
그에게 차이와 해석은 충실한 번역의 일부였다.

questions.q: 이 글의 중심 내용으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 노벨문학상 심사위원 선정 기준
번역은 치환이 아니라 두 사회를 헤아리는 판단이라는 것
영국 독립 출판사의 경영 방식
한국 문학의 해외 판매 실적
questions.explain: 글은 대응어가 없는 어휘를 어떻게 다룰지의 문제를 중심에 놓고, 번역가의 판단에는 두 사회에 대한 이해가 필요하다는 결론으로 나아간다.

questions.q: 2016년 부커상 인터내셔널 부문에 대한 설명으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 번역가에게만 상을 주었다
출판사에 상을 주었다
그해부터 작가와 번역가에게 함께 주기 시작했다
그해에 처음 만들어진 상이다
questions.explain: 글에 이 부문이 그해부터 작가와 번역가에게 상을 함께 주기 시작했다고 나온다.

questions.q: 문맥에 비추어 「종속」의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 주가 되는 것에 딸려 매여 있는 상태
여럿이 나란히 놓인 상태
빠르게 이어지는 상태
둘로 나뉘어 있는 상태
questions.explain: 번역이 원작에 종속된 작업이 아니라는 것은, 원작에 딸린 하위 작업이 아니라는 뜻이다.

questions.q: 「정보는 남지만 결은 사라진다」는 표현이 뜻하는 바로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 번역하면 문장이 길어진다는 뜻
낱말의 개수가 줄어든다는 뜻
뜻은 전달되어도 그 말에 붙은 관계와 분위기는 전해지지 않는다는 뜻
발음이 어려워진다는 뜻
questions.explain: 앞 문장에서 그런 말에는 위계와 관계, 생활 습관이 붙어 있다고 했다. 비슷한 낱말로 바꾸면 지시하는 대상은 전해져도 그 붙어 있던 것들이 떨어져 나간다는 뜻이다.

questions.q: 「채식주의자」 영어 번역을 둘러싼 논쟁을 이 글에 근거해 정리한 것으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 스미스가 모든 지적을 받아들여 번역을 철회했다
국내 학계는 번역을 문제없다고 보았고 스미스만 실수를 인정했다
쟁점은 번역가의 개입이 어디까지 허용되는가이며, 양쪽 주장이 맞섰다
쟁점은 번역가의 한국어 학습 기간이 몇 년인가였다
questions.explain: 글은 원문 훼손이라는 지적과, 글자 그대로의 번역은 불가능하므로 해석은 충실함의 일부라는 반박을 나란히 놓고, 남은 질문이 개입의 허용 범위라고 정리한다.

challenge.q: 스미스의 반박이 성립하려면 반드시 참이어야 하는 전제는?
choices: 번역가는 원작자보다 문장력이 뛰어나야 한다
두 언어 사이에 완전히 대응하는 표현이 존재하지 않는다
독자는 원작을 읽을 수 없어야 한다

en: In 2024 the novelist Han Kang received the Nobel Prize in Literature, the first Korean writer to do so. The judges of that prize cannot read Korean. What they read was the work in English and in Swedish. Before a work can cross a border, someone must write it again in another language. Translation is not a secondary step attached to an original; it is the only route by which a work meets readers around the world.

The Vegetarian was carried into English by Deborah Smith, a British translator. She read English literature at Cambridge and began learning Korean in 2010. The choice was deliberate, made because Korean literature was almost absent from English-language publishing. In 2012, in her third year of study, she began translating the novel.

Smith's role went beyond translating. She rendered about twenty pages and sent them to a small British publisher with a proposal, and the editor read the pages and decided to publish. After the book appeared she also wrote to critics and readers about it. In 2016 it won the Booker Prize International. From that year the award began to honour the writer and the translator together. It was a moment when translation was recognised as independent creative labour rather than work subordinate to an original.

The hardest point in translation is a word with no counterpart. Words such as soju, seonsaengnim, and hyeong carry a society's hierarchy, relationships, and daily habits along with them. The moment they are replaced by a similar English word, the information survives but the texture is lost. Smith chose to leave such words untranslated, keeping the Korean sounds. They remain strange sounds to a reader, and that strangeness itself becomes a marker of another society.

The translation later became the subject of debate among Korean scholars. Critics said that Korean sentences with an omitted subject had been rendered wrongly, and that sentences absent from the original had been added, changing how characters appear. Some called the result closer to a rewriting than a translation. Smith admitted some mistakes, but argued that a literal translation cannot exist at all, because two languages differ in grammar, in words, and even in the weight of their punctuation. For her, difference and interpretation were part of a faithful translation. The debate leaves one question. How far may a translator intervene?

L4.title: 존재하지 않는 자리에서 본 산 — 겸재 정선의 진경
paragraphs: 조선의 산수화는 오랫동안 중국에서 건너온 화보를 본떠 그려졌다.
화가는 중국 땅을 밟아 본 적이 없었지만 화폭에는 중국의 산수가 담겼다.
이상적인 산수의 형상이 화보 속에 이미 규정되어 있었고,
화가의 실력은 그 틀을 얼마나 능숙하게 구사하는가로 평가되었다.
그 안에 조선의 땅은 들어 있지 않았다.
그는 금강산에 오르고 인왕산 구석구석을 수없이 걸었다.
그리고 자기 눈으로 확인한 풍경을 그림의 대상으로 삼았다.
실경을 다룬 이 산수화를 진경산수라 부른다.
조선의 땅이 그림의 주인공이 된 것은 이때부터이며,
무엇을 그릴 가치가 있다고 보는가의 전환이었다.
1751년, 일흔여섯의 정선은 소나기가 지나간 인왕산을 그렸다.
비에 젖어 검게 변한 바위를 짙은 먹으로 눌러 표현했고,
산허리에는 물러가는 구름이 흰 띠로 남아 있다.
2021년 고 이건희 회장의 유족이 국립중앙박물관에 기증하면서
누구나 찾아가 볼 수 있는 그림이 되었다.
여기서 한 가지 오해를 짚어야 한다.
내금강의 봉우리들은 어느 한자리에서 한꺼번에 조망할 수 있는 대상이 아니다.

곧 이 그림은 실제로는 존재하지 않는 자리에서 본 풍경이다.
이 재구성은 사실의 훼손이 아니라 방법이다.
화가는 망막에 맺힌 상을 그대로 옮기지 않는다.
무엇을 남기고 무엇을 한자리에 모을지 판단한다.
「진경(眞景)」이라는 말 자체가 이 이중성을 품고 있다.
눈앞의 실제 경치를 뜻하는 동시에 그 경치의 참모습을 뜻하기 때문이다.

en: For a long time Joseon landscape painting followed picture books brought from China. The painter had never set foot on Chinese soil, yet Chinese scenery filled the paper. The form of an ideal landscape was already prescribed in those books, and a painter's skill was judged by how fluently he handled that pattern. Such work is called idea landscape. There were no few outstanding works, but the land of Joseon was not inside them.

Jeong Seon (1676-1759) overturned this practice. He climbed Geumgangsan and walked every corner of Inwangsan many times over. He then took as his subject the scenery his own eyes had confirmed. A landscape that deals with a real place is called jingyeong, a true view. From this point the land of Joseon became the subject of the picture, and that was more than a change of material. It was a shift in what counted as worth painting.

In 1751, at the age of seventy-six, Jeong Seon painted Inwangsan after a shower had passed. The work is Inwangjesaekdo. He pressed dark ink onto rocks the rain had turned black, and a white band of retreating cloud remains across the slope. The painting was privately owned for a long time. In 2021 the family of the late chairman Lee Kun-hee gave it to the National Museum of Korea, where it received the accession number Kunhee 1 and became a work anyone can go and see.

One misunderstanding should be addressed here. It is the idea that a true view is a kind of ancestor of the photograph. Geumgangjeondo, painted in 1734, breaks that idea. The peaks of the inner Geumgang cannot be surveyed from any single spot at one time. Jeong Seon travelled through the whole area, from Jangansa up to Birobong, then rebuilt it from a viewpoint looking down from above and placed it inside one circular composition. The picture therefore shows a scene viewed from a position that does not exist.

This rebuilding is not damage to fact but a method. A painter does not transfer the image on the retina straight to the paper. He judges what to keep and what to gather into one place. The word jingyeong itself holds this double sense, since it means the actual scene before the eyes and also the true form of that scene. What Jeong Seon tried to seize was not the outline of Inwangsan but the state of a mountain made heavy with rain. That approaching a fact still involves interpretation is the question a true view leaves behind.

L4.title: 기록은 무엇을 되살릴 수 있는지를 정한다
paragraphs: 1794년 정조는 수원에 새 성을 쌓는 공사를 시작했다.
당시로서는 막대한 경비와 기술이 투입된 대규모 토목 공사였다.
정약용은 무거운 자재를 들어 올리는 거중기와 튼튼한 수레인 유형거를 고안해
그러나 이 글에서 더 중요한 것은
정조는 공사의 전 과정을 기록으로 남기게 했다.
그렇게 편찬된 것이 「화성성역의궤」이며, 1801년에 열 권으로 인쇄되었다.
여기에는 성곽과 부속 건물의 도면이 실려 있고,
자재의 종류와 수량, 참여한 장인과 인부의 이름, 지급한 품삯,
다시 지을 수 있을 만큼 자세한 설명서였다.
이 기록의 값어치는 이백 년 뒤에 드러났다.
일제강점기와 한국전쟁을 거치며 화성의 성벽과 건물은 크게 무너졌다.
1970년대에 복원이 시작되었을 때 가장 중요한 자료가 의궤였다.
도면과 치수, 재료 목록이 남아 있었으므로
무너진 자리를 근거에 따라 되세울 수 있었다.
여기서 문화유산 복원의 원칙을 짚어야 한다.
복원은 확실한 근거 위에서만 이루어져야 하고,
근거가 끊겨 추측이 시작되는 지점에서 멈추어야 한다.
이 원칙 때문에 크게 복원한 건축물은 대개 세계유산으로 인정받기 어렵다.
무엇이 원래 모습이었는지 확인할 방법이 없으면
복원된 것은 옛것이 아니라 오늘의 상상이 되기 때문이다.
화성은 바로 이 지점에서 다른 조건에 있었다.
성과 그 성을 적은 책이 나란히 인정받은 셈이다.
기록은 지나간 일을 보존하는 데서 그치지 않는다.
무엇을 되살릴 수 있고 무엇을 영영 잃는지를 미리 정해 놓는다.
남기지 않은 것은 훗날 복원의 대상이 아니라

en: In 1794 King Jeongjo began building a new fortress at Suwon. This fortress is Hwaseong. For its time it was a large civil engineering project into which enormous funds and skill were poured. Jeong Yak-yong designed a lifting device for heavy materials and a sturdy cart, and these reduced both labour and cost. The fortress was completed in 1796. What matters more in this account, however, is what happened after the work ended.

The king had the entire process of the project set down as a record. What was compiled in this way is the Hwaseong Seongyeok Uigwe, printed in ten volumes in 1801. It carries drawings of the walls and attached buildings, the kind and quantity of materials, the names of craftsmen and labourers, the wages paid, and a daily log of the work. It was not a monument made to boast of the project. It was a manual detailed enough to build the thing again.

The worth of that record appeared two hundred years later. Through the colonial period and the Korean War the walls and buildings of Hwaseong fell into serious ruin. When restoration began in the 1970s, the Uigwe was the most important source. Because the drawings, the measurements, and the list of materials survived, the ruined parts could be raised again on evidence.

Here a principle of heritage restoration must be noted. Restoration should proceed only on firm evidence, and it must stop at the point where evidence runs out and guesswork begins. Because of this principle a heavily rebuilt structure is usually hard to recognise as World Heritage. If there is no way to confirm the original form, what is rebuilt is not the old thing but today's imagination. On exactly this point Hwaseong stood in a different position.

In 1997 Hwaseong was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list, and in 2007 the royal protocols of Joseon, the Uigwe among them, entered the Memory of the World register. The fortress and the book that described it were recognised side by side. The nature of a record shows itself here. A record does not only preserve what has passed. It decides in advance what can be brought back and what is lost for good. Whatever was not written down becomes, in a later age, not an object of restoration but an object of guesswork.

en: Newly learned material does not become a lasting memory at once. New information is first stored for a time in the hippocampus, deep inside the brain. A memory at this stage is unstable, fading easily or being pushed aside by information that arrives after it. Material crammed just before a test, and gone within days, shows this instability plainly.

The process by which an unstable short-term memory becomes a stable long-term one is called consolidation. At its core lies a change of storage place. Information placed for a time in the hippocampus gradually moves to the wide storage space of the cerebral cortex, and researchers call this systems consolidation. What matters is that the move proceeds mainly during sleep rather than while we are awake.

A sleeping brain has not stopped working. Patterns of nerve activity that appeared during learning are repeated in sleep in a form compressed in time. This is called memory reactivation and is regarded as the central mechanism of consolidation. During slow-wave sleep, the deepest stage, signals between the hippocampus and the cortex lock together and the repetition becomes especially active.

Here a common belief about learning is shaken: the belief that results depend only on the hours spent awake. Studies have confirmed again and again that restricting sleep after new learning seriously impairs consolidation. When material memorised through an all-nighter fails to last, the cause is not weak willpower but the loss of the time needed to copy it over. The amount memorised while awake and the amount that actually remains are not the same number.

This should not, however, be turned into a simple formula. The national mental health portal advises nine to ten hours of sleep a day for children and teenagers, while stating that the amount needed differs between individuals. The minimum for each person is the amount that lets them get through the next day without fatigue. Nor does sleeping longer raise grades by itself. What is clear is only this: keeping what you have learned takes time to copy it over, and closing the book is not the end of studying.

en: The way citizens take part in trials differs from country to country. Under the jury system, jurors drawn from ordinary citizens judge guilt independently of professional judges, and the judge is bound by their verdict. Under the lay judge system, lay judges sit as members of the bench itself and decide questions of fact and of law with the same authority as professional judges. Korea's citizen participation trial did not import either one as it stood. It mixed the two systems and added changes fitted to Korean conditions. What those changes are, and why they were made, reveals the character of the system.

A juror is not a volunteer. From a list of candidates drawn up in advance, the court selects as many as it needs at random and notifies them of a selection hearing. Any citizen over the age of twenty may serve without special qualification, but people with certain criminal records, and people in certain jobs such as lawyers and police officers, are excluded. The selection hearing is closed, and candidates are called by number rather than by name, a device meant to protect privacy and personal safety. The size of the jury varies with the gravity of the case. Nine jurors take part where the offence carries a possible death sentence or life imprisonment and seven in other cases, and five may be used where the defendant or counsel has admitted the main substance of the charge.

When the arguments close, the jurors enter the deliberation room. Only jurors take part, and in principle they proceed without the involvement of a judge. If all agree, that agreement stands as the verdict. If they do not agree, they must hear the opinion of the judge who heard the case before reaching a verdict, and then decide by majority. Even then the judge may not state an opinion on guilt or innocence, and having spoken may still not take part in the verdict. Where the verdict is guilty, the jurors discuss sentencing together with the judge, but they do not vote on the sentence; they may only offer an opinion. The foreperson draws up a verdict sheet separating the number of guilty opinions from the number of not-guilty opinions, collects every juror's signature, seals it, and hands it to the bench.

The force of a verdict that has come this far is nonetheless limited. The law provides that the verdict and the sentencing opinion of the jurors do not bind the court. They carry only advisory force, and the judge may hand down a judgment different from the verdict. Yet the law places one more step here. When delivering judgment the presiding judge must inform the defendant of the jurors' verdict, and where the judgment differs from the verdict, must explain the reason to the defendant. No duty to follow is imposed, but a duty to explain not following is.

Set side by side, these two provisions let us read the difficulty the drafters faced. Had the verdict been made binding, the role of judges trained in legal judgment would have been erased. Had it been left as mere reference material, a conclusion citizens spent days reaching would have vanished without a trace. Our system chose explanation over compulsion. Because the explanation is given in open court and stays on the record, a judge who overturns a verdict must have grounds ready. This choice has its price, of course. A duty to explain cannot compel a conclusion, and no standard for judging how thorough an explanation must be is written into the law. Even so, what the approach means is clear: the force that moves an institution does not always come from compulsion, and sometimes requiring reasons to be stated is enough to give a conclusion weight.

en: A road increases human movement and at the same time cuts an ecological axis. When a single road across a forest divides a habitat in two, animals are confined to a narrowed area, step onto the road in search of food and mates, and are struck by cars. The structure meant to rejoin this severed ground is the eco-corridor. Some pass beneath the road as tunnels and some cross above it as bridges; Korea's first was a tunnel laid in 1998 on provincial road 861 through Jirisan. Today the national parks hold nine tunnels and nine bridges, eighteen in all.

The National Park Research Institute, part of the Korea National Park Service, analysed those eighteen and set out the effect in figures. During the first three years an average of 522 animals a year used the corridors, and after eight years the number reached 675, a rise of about thirty percent. At the fifteen corridors more than five years old, yearly roadkill fell by an average of about eighteen percent from before construction. The tunnel built in 2013 at the Woljeongsa approach road in Odaesan recorded the highest reduction rate, 87.3 percent. Guiding fences and signboards placed beside the corridors played their part by steering animals towards them.

The passage in this material most worth attention is not the size of the effect but the moment it appeared. Wild animals do not use an unfamiliar structure straight away. The rise in crossings and the fall in accidents emerged only after several years, and the service regards the point around five years, when use stabilises, as the settling stage. Had performance been measured immediately after completion, these corridors would without exception have been recorded as having no effect. Judgment became possible only once years of observation had accumulated.

Building them, even so, is not the whole task. The Ministry of Environment surveyed every one of the country's 564 eco-corridors and then asked for improvements at 535 of them. In many cases the vegetation inside had not been properly established, or the passage doubled as a drainage channel or farm track so that its intended function weakened. If the structure stands but no animal passes through it, it is not an eco-corridor. Saying a bridge has been built and saying animals cross that bridge are not the same sentence.

Lay the two sets of findings side by side and the nature of the problem appears. Because the effect comes late, a well-built corridor measured too soon looks like a failure; and where management lapses, a corridor never works however long it stands. Either way the only answer is to keep counting. That is why the ministry has decided to strengthen advance review of installation plans, to build a system gathering corridor information, and to add a procedure for evaluation after construction. Building carries budgets and opening ceremonies with it; counting carries neither. Without counting, however, we cannot even know what has gone wrong.

paragraphs: 고고학이 다루는 연대에는 두 종류가 있다.
유물끼리 견주어 무엇이 먼저이고 무엇이 나중인지를 세우는 상대연대와,
몇 년의 것인지를 못 박는 절대연대다.
발굴 현장에서 얻기 쉬운 쪽은 앞의 것이다.

벽돌을 쌓아 만든 무덤 하나가 우연히 드러났다.
중국 남조 양나라의 영향이 뚜렷한 양식이었다.
널길 가운데에 돌짐승이 남쪽을 향해 서 있었고,
그 앞에 납작한 돌판 두 장이 나란히 놓여 있었다.
지신에게서 무덤 쓸 땅을 사들였다는 문서로,
삼국시대 능에서 발견된 매지권은 지금까지 이것뿐이다.
이 두 장이 해낸 일은 두 겹이다.
먼저 무덤 주인이 백제 무령왕임을 입증했다.
주인을 확정할 수 있는 무덤은 이곳이 유일하다.
다음으로 무덤을 쌓은 연대를 알려 주었고,
그 결과 함께 묻힌 유물들의 제작 시기까지 정해졌다.
연도를 아는 유물 한 무더기가 한꺼번에 생긴 것이다.
이 유물들은 그 뒤 다른 무덤의 비슷한 물건을 재는 자가 되어,
어떻게 변해 왔는지를 살피는 기준 자료로 쓰인다.
얼마나 우연에 기대고 있는지도 함께 보아야 한다.
이 무덤은 도굴되지 않은 채 남았고,
학자들이 찾아낸 것이 아니라 배수로 공사 중에 드러났으며,
죽은 이의 이름과 날짜를 돌에 새겨 넣는 풍습이 있었다.
그리고 기준에 기대는 만큼 위험도 함께 온다.
이 무덤의 연대 위에 세운 다른 연대들은
천오백 년 뒤의 학문이 자를 갖게 되었다.
