en: The dates archaeology works with come in two kinds. There is relative dating, which compares objects and establishes which came earlier and which later, and absolute dating, which fixes the year an object belongs to. The former is the easier to obtain in the field. Grouping similar shapes and setting them in order becomes possible once enough objects have been gathered. Yet how many centuries that whole line spans remains unknown. Only when an object appears that drives a dated nail into the line does a chronology take shape.

In 1971, while a drainage ditch was being dug in Gongju, a tomb built of bricks came to light by chance. Its style bore the clear influence of the Liang dynasty of southern China. A stone beast stood facing south in the middle of the passage, and in front of it lay two flat stone tablets side by side. They were memorial tablets of blue-grey stone, roughly 41.5 by 35 centimetres, with characters carved in regular script.

The text read as follows. The king's tablet recorded that King Sama of Baekje, Great General Yeongdong, died on the seventh day of the fifth month of 523 at the age of sixty-two and was laid in the great tomb on the twelfth day of the eighth month of 525. The front of the queen's tablet recorded that she died in the twelfth month of 526 and was laid to rest on the twelfth day of the second month of 529, once the three-year mourning was over; the back was a land-purchase deed. It states that on the twelfth day of the eighth month of 525 the ground for the tomb was bought from the earth god for ten thousand coins, and it remains the only such deed found in a tomb of the Three Kingdoms period.

What these two stones achieved has two layers. First, they proved that the owner of the tomb was King Muryeong of Baekje. Tombs of the Three Kingdoms period are countless, but this is the only one whose occupant can be identified with certainty. Second, they gave the year the tomb was built, and with it the time of making of every object buried alongside. A whole set of dated objects came into being at once. Those objects have since served as a ruler for measuring similar things from other tombs, and are used as reference material for tracing how the styles of Baekje tombs and metal craftwork changed.

We should also see, however, how much this seemingly solid fixed point rests on chance. The tomb survived without being robbed; it was uncovered not by searching scholars but during work on a drainage ditch; and above all, the people of Baekje at that time had the custom of carving the name and dates of the dead into stone. Had any one of the three gone otherwise, this fixed point would not exist. And leaning on a standard brings its own risk. Other dates built upon the date of this tomb will shift if that standard shifts. One thing is nonetheless clear: because someone wrote down the dates, the scholarship of fifteen centuries later has a ruler.

questions.q: 글쓴이가 마지막에 무령왕릉의 지석을 다시 불러온 까닭으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 돌에 새기는 방식으로 돌아가자고 제안하려고
옛 기록이 더 훌륭했음을 보이려고
지석이 국보임을 알리려고
돌보지 않아도 남는 기록과 돌봐야만 남는 기록을 맞세워 오늘의 조건을 드러내려고
questions.explain: 천오백 년을 스스로 견딘 기록과, 손을 놓으면 곧 사라지는 기록을 나란히 놓아 오늘의 보존이 어떤 일인지를 부각한다.

challenge.q: 이 글의 논지에 비추어 가장 위험한 상황은?
choices: 보존 포맷이 국제 표준으로 승인되는 것
보존매체를 원본과 복본 두 벌로 나누는 것
기록을 옮길 때마다 전자서명을 새로 붙이는 것
예산이 줄어 매체변환과 포맷 변환이 몇 해 동안 멈추는 것
challenge.explain: 글은 예산과 인력이 끊기면 보존이 즉시 멈추고, 멈춘 기록은 몇 해 안에 열 수 없게 된다고 밝힌다.

challenge.q: 이 글의 원리를 학교 기록물 관리에 적용한 예로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 가장 최신 프로그램의 전용 형식으로 모아 두고 그대로 둔다
공개 표준 형식으로 저장하고, 주기적으로 매체를 옮기며 원본과 사본을 나누어 둔다
자료를 한 사람의 컴퓨터에만 모아 둔다
해마다 자료를 새로 만들고 옛 자료는 지운다
challenge.explain: 공개 표준·주기적 매체 이전·원본과 복본 분리는 이 글이 설명한 국가기록원의 방식 그대로다.

en: Preservation is commonly understood as leaving something alone. Letters carved in stone fit that understanding: no one tended them, yet they are read fifteen centuries later. With digital records the understanding is turned entirely upside down. Because a copy loses nothing, it seems that one saving will last for ever; in practice decay begins the moment hands are taken off. It is faster than paper, and beyond comparison with stone.

There are two paths to loss. The first is the ageing of the medium. A disk on which a record was written becomes unreadable with time. The second is the disappearance of the format. A file tied to a particular program has its contents locked inside the moment that program is gone. The bits are intact while the means of reading them is not, which is closer to total loss than damage would be.

The response is conversion in two directions: media conversion, moving records from an aged medium onto a new one, and format conversion, changing a format nearing the end of its life into one that will last. When the National Archives of Korea selects a preservation medium it weighs lifespan and durability, large capacity and low cost, and how broadly the medium is used. Formats are not picked arbitrarily either. Candidates were compared against nine criteria, among them whether the format is an open standard, how widespread it is, whether it is stable, whether it can carry descriptive information and whether it protects authenticity. PDF/A was chosen as the document preservation format. Approved as an international standard in 2005, it is owned by a standards body rather than any single company, so anyone may use it without payment, and that proved decisive.

Here the paradox of preservation appears. A record survives only by being copied onward, yet each copying sharpens the question of whether what exists now is what was first made. The long-term preservation format is the answer to that question. The original record, the version converted into the document preservation format and the metadata are packaged and kept together, so that what came before a move is held beside what came after it, rather than the result alone. On top of this, at each transfer from the producing body to the records office and on to the permanent archives, a fresh electronic signature is attached, proving authenticity in an unbroken line.

Running preservation media in two sets follows the same design. The medium that counts as the original is isolated in a separate repository and used as little as possible, while a duplicate that can absorb wear is used for consultation and distribution. All these procedures point to one conclusion. Digital preservation is not storage but labour. It stops the instant budget and staff stop, and a record left stopped becomes unopenable within a few years. The memorial stone of King Muryeong endured fifteen centuries that nobody tended; the records we make today reach tomorrow only if someone keeps working on them.

L4.title: 추천 알고리즘과 필터버블

questions.q: 이 글의 핵심 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 추천 알고리즘은 사생활을 침해하므로 금지해야 한다.
필터버블은 근거가 전혀 없는 개념으로 밝혀졌다.
온라인 플랫폼은 모든 이용자에게 같은 화면을 보여 준다.
개인화 추천은 편리하지만 필터버블을 부를 수 있어 균형 잡힌 이용 태도가 필요하다.
questions.explain: 글은 개인화 추천의 원리와 편리함, 필터버블의 위험을 차례로 설명한 뒤 이용자의 균형 잡힌 태도가 중요하다고 마무리하고 있다.

questions.q: 이 글에서 추천 알고리즘이 활용한다고 언급한 정보가 아닌 것은?
choices: 시청 기록
이용자의 얼굴 표정
검색어
'좋아요'와 같은 행동 데이터
questions.explain: 첫째 문단에서 알고리즘은 시청 기록, 검색어, '좋아요'와 같은 행동 데이터를 수집한다고 했을 뿐, 얼굴 표정은 언급하지 않았다.

questions.q: '정보 편식'의 문맥상 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 자신의 입맛에 맞는 정보만 치우치게 받아들이는 것
정보를 여러 사람에게 고르게 나누어 주는 것
음식에 관한 정보를 즐겨 찾아보는 것
정보를 오랫동안 기억하지 못하는 것
questions.explain: 좋아하는 음식만 가려 먹는 '편식'에 빗대어, 보고 싶은 정보만 골라 접하는 태도를 정보 편식이라고 표현한 것이다.

questions.q: 이 글에 나타난 글쓴이의 관점으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 기술이 발전하면 필터버블 문제는 저절로 사라질 것이다.
플랫폼 기업이 추천 기능을 없애는 것이 유일한 해결책이다.
문제 해결의 열쇠는 기술 자체보다 기술을 이해하고 활용하는 이용자의 태도에 있다.
확증 편향은 개인의 노력으로는 극복할 수 없다.
questions.explain: 셋째 문단에서 글쓴이는 알고리즘 자체가 나쁜 것이 아니라며 다양한 정보 접하기와 디지털 리터러시 등 이용자의 태도를 해법으로 제시하고 있다.
